name: Rizatriptan
route_note: Oral tablets and orally disintegrating wafers.

discovery.by: Merck Sharp & Dohme research laboratories (Terlings Park, UK)
discovery.note: A triazolylmethyl indole triptan designed for better oral absorption than sumatriptan. Year of the first patent, per Wikipedia (patented 1991, medical use 1998).

tagline: Fast-acting oral triptan for acute migraine, including in adolescents
summary: Rizatriptan is a second-generation triptan with higher oral bioavailability and faster onset than oral sumatriptan. It is used for acute migraine in adults and children aged 6 and older.
mechanism: Like other triptans, rizatriptan stimulates 5-HT1B receptors on cranial blood vessels (vasoconstriction) and 5-HT1D receptors on trigeminal afferents (inhibiting CGRP and neuropeptide release), aborting the migraine attack.
uses: Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults and children aged 6–17

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Maxalt and the orally disintegrating Maxalt-MLT.

history.title: Meta-analysis
history.detail: A meta-analysis of 53 triptan trials (Ferrari et al., Lancet) ranks rizatriptan 10 mg among the most effective oral triptans.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: The FDA approves rizatriptan for migraine in patients aged 6–17, the first triptan for children this young.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic rizatriptan becomes available in the US.

history.title: Organon
history.detail: Merck spins off Organon, which takes over Maxalt and other established brands.

pk.excretion: renal, mainly as indole acetic acid metabolite

facts: Propranolol raises rizatriptan concentrations by about 70%, so a lower dose is labelled for people taking it.
